ladder.classBlurb: The Artificer learns to build with fog and reflection, making devices that exist in two places or show what is hidden.
The Artificer files patents with devils and angels, building engines powered by signed contracts and sung hymns.
The Artificer's machines stop following plans and start improvising, rebuilding themselves mid-battle into whatever is needed.
The Artificer builds for crushing depth and darkness, crafting armour and vessels nothing below can break.
The Artificer's machines become half alive, grown rather than built, with gears that heal and remember.
The Artificer builds vessels that sail between strange stars and wide horizons, carrying whole armies across realms.
The Artificer learns to build with absence itself, making devices with no weight, no sound and no way to be stopped.
The Artificer builds devices so strange that the world forgets them as soon as they leave, yet they keep working.
The Artificer works raw Law like clay, building tools that shape the first stuff of the world. Still mortal, but their works outlast gods.

subclasses.ds: A tinkerer who trades grounded machinery for lift and drift, gaining a stored charge that powers hover and flight tricks other Artificers can't.
Artificers who create potions and reagents through experimental science. (Tasha's Cauldron of Everything)
Artificers who build a magical suit of armor and fight in it. (Tasha's Cauldron of Everything)
Artificers who deploy magical cannons. (Tasha's Cauldron of Everything)
Artificers who fight alongside a steel defender. (Tasha's Cauldron of Everything)
An artificer who weaponises disease and infection, turning biological processes into armaments.
An artificer who etches power into gear rather than building it in, granting temporary magical properties to weapons and armor.
An artificer who powers constructs with captured fragments of spirit rather than raw mechanism.

ladder.classBlurb: The Barbarian's rage rolls out like fog, hiding them and confusing every enemy that hears their roar.
The Barbarian's rage becomes holy and hellish fire at once, burning the body forward through any wound.
The Barbarian's fury breaks the rules of the world, warping the ground and tossing enemies wherever it likes.
The Barbarian grows vast and heavy like a creature from the deep, rage as crushing as the bottom of the sea.
The Barbarian draws on the rage of every ancestor in their blood, each ring of their life adding another body's strength.
The Barbarian becomes a giant of far horizons, leaping across battlefields and shattering mountains under strange stars.
The Barbarian's rage empties them of fear, pain and hesitation until only the act of destruction remains.
The Barbarian becomes rage that the world can no longer remember, striking from places foes forgot to watch.
The Barbarian embodies the first anger of the world, the rage of storms and earthquakes before anything had a name.

subclasses.ds: A barbarian who grows and hardens by spending their own blood, trading hit points for damage resistance and raw size.
A barbarian who rages to destroy, not just to fight, leaving wrecked terrain and prone enemies in their wake.
Barbarians whose rage leaks raw, unpredictable magic. (Tasha's Cauldron of Everything)
Barbarians who call on the spirits of their ancestors to shield their allies. (Xanathar's Guide to Everything)
Armored brawlers who fight in spiked armor. (Originally dwarf-only in the book; many tables drop that restriction.) (Sword Coast Adventurer's Guide)
Barbarians whose rage reveals a bestial form within. (Tasha's Cauldron of Everything)
The simplest, most violent barbarian path — rage turned into more damage and more attacks, at the cost of vulnerability once it ends.
Barbarians who draw on the might of giants. (Bigby Presents: Glory of the Giants)
A barbarian whose rage summons a storm aura — this vault leans on the Sea variant. (Xanathar's Guide to Everything)
A barbarian who channels an animal spirit — bear, eagle, or wolf — into their rage. (Player's Handbook)
Barbarians who draw on the cosmic tree whose roots and branches connect the realms. (Player's Handbook (2024))
A barbarian whose rage is religious fervor, empowered by a god and hard to put down. (Xanathar's Guide to Everything)
A barbarian whose rage calls down lightning rather than just muscle, arcing bolts to nearby foes mid-swing.

ladder.classBlurb: The Bard learns songs that lead listeners astray, weaving mist and false paths with every verse.
The Bard sings in both the infernal and heavenly tongues, a voice that can bargain with devils and stir angels.
The Bard's music turns wild, a symphony that can scramble enemy minds and the battlefield itself.
The Bard sings so low the deep answers, songs that echo up from the dark and bring the fear of drowning.
The Bard learns the songs of memory, singing ages back into being and making the past answer for itself.
The Bard sings to far horizons, songs that travel across worlds and bring allies from impossible distances.
The Bard learns the song of nothing, music made of pauses that steals the power of anything it touches.
The Bard sings songs that erase themselves, leaving listeners changed without knowing why.
The Bard sings the song the world was shaped to, a mortal voice that can still move the old Laws.

subclasses.ds: A bard who performs funeral rites and battlefield dirges, steadying allies while unsettling the dying.
Bards who channel the song that shaped the world. (Tasha's Cauldron of Everything)
Bards whose performance is movement: dancers who fight as they perform. (Player's Handbook (2024))
A bard who plays on sleep and dream rather than waking emotion, drowsing enemies and walking into their nightmares.
A bard whose magic repeats and layers rather than striking once, echoing spells onto second targets.
Masters of oratory and persuasion. (Tasha's Cauldron of Everything)
Bards who wield fey enchantment — beauty, charm, and command. (Xanathar's Guide to Everything)
A bard who collects secrets and knowledge rather than fighting spirit — versatile magic and social utility over any single trick.
Storytellers who channel spirits through their tales. (Van Richten's Guide to Ravenloft)
Blade-dancing performers who fight as they entertain. (Xanathar's Guide to Everything)
Battle-poets who inspire allies from the front lines. (Player's Handbook)
Bards who trade in fear, secrets, and stolen identities. (Xanathar's Guide to Everything)
A bard who specialises in the music of war — battle hymns, war drums, and the songs that drive armies forward.
